instruction: In the Reserve Bank of India Annual Report 2025-26, what real GDP growth is projected for India for 2026-27?
response: Real GDP growth for 2026-27 is projected at 6.9 per cent with risks tilted to the downside.
evidence: at 6.9 per cent with risks

instruction: Under SEBI's ICDR Regulations, 2018, who qualifies as an anchor investor in a main board public issue?
response: An anchor investor is a qualified institutional buyer who applies for a value of at least ten crore rupees in a main board public issue made through book building.
evidence: means a qualified institutional buyer who makes an application for a value of at least ten crore rupees in a public issue on the main board

instruction: How do the SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018 define a qualified institutions placement?
response: It is an issue of eligible securities by a listed issuer to qualified institutional buyers on a private placement basis. It also covers an offer for sale of specified securities by the promoters or promoter group on a private placement basis.
evidence: means issue of eligible securities by a listed issuer to qualified institutional buyers on a private placement basis

instruction: Under SEBI's ICDR Regulations, 2018, when is an issuer ineligible to make an initial public offer because of outstanding convertible securities, and what is excepted?
response: An issuer cannot make an initial public offer if any convertible securities or other rights entitle a person to receive its equity shares. Exceptions include outstanding employee stock options granted under a compliant scheme, and fully paid-up convertible securities that must be converted by the date of filing the red herring prospectus or prospectus.
evidence: An issuer shall not be eligible to make an initial public offer if there are any outstanding convertible securities or any other right which would entitle any person with any option to receive equity shares of the issuer

instruction: What net tangible assets must an issuer have to be eligible for an initial public offer on the main board under SEBI's ICDR Regulations, 2018, and what limit applies to monetary assets?
response: It must have net tangible assets of at least three crore rupees in each of the preceding three full years, on a restated and consolidated basis. Not more than fifty per cent of these may be held in monetary assets, unless the excess has been used or firmly committed to be used in the business or project.
evidence: net tangible assets of at least three crore rupees, calculated on a restated and consolidated basis, in each of the preceding three full years

instruction: Under SEBI's ICDR Regulations, 2018, what average operating profit must an issuer have to be eligible to make an initial public offer?
response: An issuer must have an average operating profit of at least fifteen crore rupees during the preceding three years, calculated on a restated and consolidated basis, with operating profit in each of those three years.
evidence: it has an average operating profit of at least fifteen crore rupees, calculated on a restated and consolidated basis, during the preceding three years

instruction: Under SEBI's ICDR Regulations, 2018, what must an issuer that does not meet the main board IPO track record conditions do to make an initial public offer?
response: It may proceed only through the book-building process, and it must undertake to allot at least seventy five per cent of the net offer to qualified institutional buyers and refund the full subscription money if it fails to do so.
evidence: the issuer undertakes to allot at least seventy five per cent. of the net offer to qualified institutional buyers and to refund the full subscription money if it fails to do so

instruction: Under SEBI's ICDR Regulations, 2018, what range of voting rights ratio may SR equity shares carry compared to ordinary shares for an issuer listing on the Main Board?
response: SR equity shares must carry voting rights in a ratio from a minimum of 2:1 up to a maximum of 10:1 compared to ordinary shares, and the ratio must be in whole numbers only.
evidence: voting rights in the ratio of a minimum of 2:1 upto a maximum of 10:1 compared to ordinary shares

instruction: Under SEBI's ICDR Regulations, 2018, what cap applies to the amount for general corporate purposes in a main board initial public offer?
response: The amount for general corporate purposes stated in the objects of the issue in the draft offer document and offer document cannot exceed twenty five per cent of the amount being raised by the issuer.
evidence: The amount for general corporate purposes, as mentioned in objects of the issue in the draft offer document and the offer document shall not exceed twenty five per cent. of the amount being raised by the issuer.

instruction: Under SEBI's ICDR Regulations, 2018, what firm financing arrangement must an issuer have for a specific project funded from IPO proceeds?
response: The issuer must have made firm arrangements of finance through verifiable means for seventy five per cent of the stated means of finance, excluding the amount raised through the public issue or existing identifiable internal accruals.
evidence: it has made firm arrangements of finance through verifiable means towards seventy five per cent. of the stated means of finance for a specific project

instruction: Under SEBI's ICDR Regulations, 2018, how long must equity shares have been held by sellers before they can be offered for sale in an initial public offer, and what happens with convertible securities?
response: Shares must have been held for at least one year before the draft offer document is filed. Where shares come from conversion of fully paid-up compulsorily convertible securities, the holding period of the convertible securities and the resulting shares together is counted toward the one year.
evidence: Only such fully paid-up equity shares may be offered for sale to the public, which have been held by the sellers for a period of at least one year prior to the filing of the draft offer document

instruction: Under SEBI's ICDR Regulations, 2018, what share of post-issue capital must promoters hold in a main board initial public offer, and how can a shortfall be covered?
response: The promoters must hold at least twenty per cent of the post-issue capital. If their holding is lower, specified investors such as alternative investment funds, banks, public financial institutions or insurance companies may cover the shortfall, up to ten per cent of post-issue capital, without being identified as promoters.
evidence: The promoters of the issuer shall hold at least twenty per cent. of the post-issue capital

instruction: Under SEBI's ICDR Regulations, 2018, what lock-in period applies to the minimum promoters' contribution if most of the IPO proceeds, excluding the offer for sale, go to capital expenditure?
response: The lock-in period is three years from the date of allotment in the initial public offer, instead of the standard eighteen months.
evidence: then the lock-in period shall be three years from the date of allotment in the initial public offer.

instruction: Under SEBI's ICDR Regulations, 2018, when is an issuer ineligible to make a rights issue because of trading suspension?
response: An issuer is ineligible if its equity shares are suspended from trading as a disciplinary measure as on the reference date.
evidence: if the equity shares of the issuer are suspended from trading as a disciplinary measure as on the reference date

instruction: Under SEBI's ICDR Regulations, 2018, what restriction applies to promoters renouncing rights in a rights issue when the issuer or its promoters or directors is a wilful defaulter or fraudulent borrower?
response: The promoters or promoter group may not renounce their rights, except to the extent of renunciation within the promoter group or to specific investors disclosed by the issuer under the regulations.
evidence: the promoters or promoter group of the issuer shall not renounce their rights except to the extent of renunciation within the promoter group

instruction: What conditions do SEBI's ICDR Regulations, 2018 set for warrants issued in a rights issue?
response: Warrant tenure cannot exceed eighteen months from allotment, and at least twenty-five per cent of the consideration based on the exercise price must be received upfront. If the holder does not exercise the option within three months from the date of payment of consideration, that consideration is forfeited by the issuer.
evidence: the tenure of such warrants shall not exceed eighteen months from their date of allotment in the rights issue

instruction: Under SEBI's ICDR Regulations, 2018, what happens if an issuer withdraws a rights issue after announcing the record date?
response: The issuer cannot withdraw the rights issue after announcing the record date. If it does, it may not apply for listing of any of its specified securities on any stock exchange for twelve months from the record date, though it may seek listing of equity shares from earlier conversions, ESOPs or warrant exercises.
evidence: The issuer shall not withdraw its rights issue after announcement of the record date.

instruction: Under SEBI's ICDR Regulations, 2018, what approval from holders is needed to roll over the non-convertible portion of partly convertible debt instruments exceeding ten crore rupees?
response: Seventy five per cent of the holders, in value, of the convertible debt instruments must approve the rollover through a resolution passed by postal ballot.
evidence: seventy five per cent. of the holders (in value) of the convertible debt instruments of the issuer have, through a resolution, approved the rollover through postal ballot

instruction: Under SEBI's ICDR Regulations, 2018, how must an issuer in a further public offer treat a name change in the last one year?
response: If the issuer changed its name in the last one year before filing the relevant offer document, it may make a further public offer only if at least fifty per cent of the revenue for the preceding one full year came from the activity indicated by its new name.
evidence: such an issuer shall make further public offer if at least fifty per cent. of the revenue for the preceding one full year has been earned by it from the activity indicated by its new name.

instruction: Under SEBI's ICDR Regulations, 2018, who cannot receive a preferential issue of specified securities because of earlier sales of the issuer's equity shares?
response: A preferential issue cannot be made to any person who sold or transferred equity shares of the issuer during the 90 trading days preceding the relevant date.
evidence: shall not be made to any person who has sold or transferred any equity shares of the issuer during the

instruction: Under SEBI's ICDR Regulations, 2018, for how long are promoters ineligible for a preferential issue after failing to exercise warrants they subscribed to?
response: The promoters and promoter group are ineligible for a preferential issue of that issuer's specified securities for one year, counted from the expiry of the warrants' tenure or from their cancellation.
evidence: the promoter(s) and promoter group shall be ineligible for issue of specified securities of such issuer on preferential basis for a period of one year

instruction: Under SEBI's ICDR Regulations, 2018, how is the relevant date fixed for a preferential issue of equity shares?
response: It is the date thirty days before the date on which the shareholders' meeting is held to consider the proposed preferential issue. If that day is a weekend or holiday, the preceding day is used.
evidence: the date thirty days prior to the date on which the meeting of shareholders is held to consider the proposed preferential issue

instruction: Under SEBI's ICDR Regulations, 2018, when must the use of proceeds of a preferential issue be monitored by a credit rating agency?
response: When the issue size exceeds one hundred crore rupees, the issuer must arrange for a registered credit rating agency to monitor the use of proceeds. This does not apply to issues by a bank, public financial institution or insurance company.
evidence: If the issue size exceeds one hundred crore rupees, the issuer shall make arrangements for the use of proceeds of the issue to be monitored by a credit rating agency registered with the Board

instruction: Under SEBI's ICDR Regulations, 2018, how long must equity shares have been listed before an issuer can make a qualified institutions placement?
response: Equity shares of the same class must have been listed on a stock exchange for at least one year before the notice to shareholders for the meeting to pass the special resolution is issued.
evidence: have been listed on a stock exchange for a period of at least one year prior to the date of issuance of notice to its shareholders for convening the meeting to pass the special resolution

instruction: Under SEBI's ICDR Regulations, 2018, what discount is permitted on the floor price in a qualified institutions placement?
response: The issuer may offer a discount of not more than five per cent on the calculated price, subject to shareholder approval, except for promoters' offers for sale made for minimum public shareholding compliance.
evidence: the issuer may offer a discount of not more than five per cent. on the price so calculated

instruction: Under SEBI's ICDR Regulations, 2018, what minimum allotment must go to mutual funds in a qualified institutions placement?
response: A minimum of ten per cent of the eligible securities must be allotted to mutual funds, and any unsubscribed part may go to other qualified institutional buyers.
evidence: minimum of ten per cent. of eligible securities shall be allotted to mutual funds

instruction: Under SEBI's ICDR Regulations, 2018, what minimum number of allottees and single-allottee limit apply to a qualified institutions placement?
response: At least two allottees are needed if the issue size is up to two hundred and fifty crore rupees, and at least five if it is larger. No single allottee may receive more than fifty per cent of the issue size.
evidence: five, where the issue size is greater than two hundred and fifty crore rupees

instruction: Under SEBI's ICDR Regulations, 2018, what happens once a bonus issue has been announced?
response: A bonus issue, once announced, cannot be withdrawn.
evidence: A bonus issue, once announced, shall not be withdrawn.

instruction: Under SEBI's ICDR Regulations, 2018, what post-issue paid-up capital limit makes an issuer eligible for an SME initial public offer?
response: An issuer is eligible only if its post-issue paid-up capital is less than or equal to ten crore rupees, though an issuer with more than ten crore and up to twenty five crore rupees may also issue under the chapter.
evidence: An issuer shall be eligible to make an initial public offer only if its post-issue paid-up capital is less than or equal to ten crore rupees.

instruction: Under SEBI's ICDR Regulations, 2018, what limit applies to the offer for sale by selling shareholders in an SME initial public offer?
response: The size of the offer for sale by selling shareholders cannot exceed twenty per cent of the total issue size.
evidence: the size of offer for sale by selling shareholders shall not exceed twenty per cent of the total issue size

instruction: On what grounds may SEBI relax strict enforcement of a requirement of the ICDR Regulations, 2018?
response: SEBI may relax a requirement in the interest of investors or market development if the requirement is procedural, a disclosure is not relevant for a class of industry or issuer, or non-compliance was caused by factors beyond the issuer's control.
evidence: the requirement is procedural in nature

instruction: Under the book building process in the SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018, how far above the floor of the price band may the cap be?
response: The cap of the price band must not be higher than the floor by more than 20 per cent., so it must be at most 120 per cent. of the floor.
evidence: The cap of the price band should not be higher by more than 20 per cent. of the floor of the band

instruction: In the SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018, what is the minimum level of the cap of a price band relative to the floor price?
response: The cap of the price band must be at least one hundred and five per cent of the floor price.
evidence: the cap of the price band shall be at least one hundred and five per cent of the floor price.

instruction: Under the SEBI ICDR Regulations' book building schedule, by how much may a price band be revised during the bidding period?
response: The maximum revision on either side is 20 per cent., meaning the floor of the band can move up or down by up to 20 per cent. of the floor disclosed in the red herring prospectus.
evidence: the maximum revision on either side shall not exceed 20 per cent.

instruction: Under the SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018, how must the bidding period be extended when the price band is revised, and what is the overall limit?
response: The issuer must extend the bidding period by at least three working days after a price band revision. The total bidding period may not exceed ten working days.
evidence: the issuer shall extend the bidding (issue) period disclosed in the red herring prospectus, for a minimum period of three working days, subject to the total bidding (issue) period not exceeding ten working days.

instruction: Under the SEBI ICDR Regulations, what is the minimum application value for an anchor investor in a main board public issue made through book building?
response: An anchor investor must apply for a value of at least ten crore rupees in a main board public issue made through the book building process.
evidence: An anchor investor shall make an application of a value of at least ten crore rupees in a public issue on the main board made through the book building process

instruction: Under the SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018, how much of the qualified institutional buyer portion can be allocated to anchor investors?
response: Up to sixty per cent. of the portion available for allocation to qualified institutional buyers can be allocated to anchor investors as the anchor investor portion.
evidence: Up to sixty per cent. of the portion available for allocation to qualified institutional buyers shall be available for allocation/allotment

instruction: Under the SEBI ICDR Regulations, what share of the anchor investor portion is reserved, and for which investors?
response: Forty per cent of the anchor investor portion is reserved: 33.33 per cent for domestic mutual funds and 6.67 per cent for life insurance companies and pension funds. Any under-subscription in the insurance and pension fund reservation may be allocated to domestic mutual funds.

instruction: Under the SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018, when does bidding by anchor investors open relative to the issue opening date?
response: Bidding for anchor investors opens one day before the issue opening date.
evidence: The bidding for anchor investors shall open one day before the issue opening date.

instruction: Under the SEBI ICDR Regulations, what lock-in applies to shares allotted to anchor investors?
response: Fifty per cent of the shares allotted to anchor investors are locked in for 90 days from allotment, and the remaining fifty per cent are locked in for 30 days from allotment.
evidence: There shall be a lock-in of 90 days on fifty per cent of the shares allotted to the anchor investors from the date of allotment, and a lock-in of 30 days on the remaining fifty per cent

instruction: Under the SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018, what happens if the book-built price is lower than the price at which anchor investors were allocated shares?
response: The excess amount is not refunded to the anchor investor. The anchor investor is allotted the securities at the same price at which the allocation was made to it. If the book-built price is higher, the anchor investor pays the additional amount.
evidence: if the price fixed as a result of book building is lower than the price at which the allocation is made to the anchor investors, the excess amount shall not be refunded to the anchor investors

instruction: Under the SEBI ICDR Regulations' book building schedule, what may the draft red herring prospectus state about the issue size and what must it leave out?
response: It must state the total issue size, as a total amount to be raised or a number of specified securities, and it must not contain the price of the specified securities.
evidence: The draft red herring prospectus shall contain the total issue size which may be expressed either in terms of the total amount to be raised or the total number of specified securities to be issued.

instruction: Under the SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018, who must underwrite a book-built issue, and what is the role of syndicate members?
response: The lead manager(s) must compulsorily underwrite the issue, and the syndicate member(s) sub-underwrite with the lead manager(s).
evidence: The lead manager(s) shall compulsorily underwrite the issue and the syndicate member(s) shall sub-underwrite with the lead manager(s).

instruction: Under the SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018, when may an issuer extend the bidding period in cases other than a price band revision?
response: In case of force majeure, banking strike or similar unforeseen circumstances, the issuer may extend the bidding period by at least one working day, for reasons recorded in writing. The total bidding period still cannot exceed ten working days.
evidence: the issuer may, for reasons to be recorded in writing, extend the bidding/issue period for a minimum period of

instruction: Under the SEBI ICDR Regulations' book building schedule, in what order must risk factors in an offer document be disclosed?
response: Risk factors must be disclosed in descending order of materiality.
evidence: Risk factors shall be disclosed in the descending order of materiality.

instruction: Under Schedule VI of the SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018, what is said about forward-looking statements in an offer document?
response: There must be no forward-looking statements that cannot be substantiated.
evidence: There shall be no forward-looking statements that cannot be substantiated.

instruction: Under the SEBI ICDR Regulations' schedule on public communications, what must a public communication say about incentives to investors?
response: No public information about the issue may contain any offer of incentives to investors, whether direct or indirect, in cash, kind, services or otherwise.
evidence: No public information with respect to the issue shall contain any offer of incentives, to the investors whether direct or indirect, in any manner

instruction: Under the SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018, whose approval must an issuer obtain for all issue advertisements and public communications?
response: The issuer must obtain approval from the lead manager(s) responsible for marketing the issue and provide copies of all issue related materials to all lead manager(s).
evidence: the issuer shall obtain the approval from the lead manager(s) responsible for marketing the issue

instruction: Under the SEBI ICDR Regulations, how must an issuer disclose material developments between filing the offer document and allotment?
response: The issuer must make prompt, true and fair disclosure of all material developments with a material effect on it. It does so through public notices in all the newspapers in which it released the pre-issue advertisement.
evidence: The issuer shall make a prompt, true and fair disclosure of all material developments which take place between the date of filing offer document and the date of allotment of specified securities

instruction: Under the SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018, when is an issuer's advertisement considered misleading regarding past performance?
response: An advertisement is misleading if it inaccurately portrays past performance, or portrays it in a way that implies past gains or income will be repeated in the future.
evidence: An inaccurate portrayal of past performance or its portrayal in a manner which implies that past gains or income will be repeated in the future.

instruction: Under the SEBI ICDR Regulations' schedule on changes in the offer document, what increase in estimated deployment in any object of the issue requires a fresh draft offer document filing?
response: Any increase in estimated deployment in any of the objects of the issue by more than twenty per cent. requires fresh filing of the draft offer document with the Board, along with fees.
evidence: Any increase in estimated deployment in any of the objects of the issue by more than twenty per cent.

instruction: Under the SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018, what change in an offer for sale requires a fresh draft offer document filing?
response: In an offer for sale, any increase or decrease of more than fifty per cent. in either the number of shares offered or the estimated issue size, as disclosed in the draft offer document, requires fresh filing.
evidence: In case of an offer for sale: any increase or decrease in either the number of shares offered for sale or the estimated issue size

instruction: Under the SEBI ICDR Regulations, what variation in net profit after tax requires filing an updated offer document with fees?
response: Any variation in net profit after tax or net loss, or in extraordinary items, in excess of 10 per cent. over the last updated financials in the draft offer document requires filing an updated offer document.
evidence: Any variation in net profit after tax or net loss and/ or extraordinary items in excess of 10 per cent. over the last updated financials included in the draft offer document.

instruction: Under the SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018, what increase in promoter shareholding triggers filing an updated offer document with fees under the capital structure heading?
response: An aggregate increase of 5 per cent. or more in the shareholding of the promoter or promoter group, or of the top ten shareholders, triggers filing of an updated offer document with fees.
evidence: An aggregate increase of 5 per cent. or more in the shareholding of the promoter or promoter group

instruction: Under the SEBI ICDR Regulations' listing schedule, what must an issuer do if it fails to apply for listing in time or listing permission is not received?
response: The securities are not eligible for listing. The issuer must immediately refund the subscription monies to the allottees, with penal interest at fifteen per cent. per annum for each day of delay from the date of allotment.
evidence: the issuer shall be liable to refund the subscription monies, if any, to the respective allottees immediately, along with penal interest for each day of delay at the rate of fifteen per cent. per annum from the date of allotment.

instruction: Under the SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018, how long does a stock exchange have to grant in-principle approval or list securities, or reject the application?
response: The stock exchange must decide within thirty days from the later of the receipt of the application or the receipt of the issuer's satisfactory reply to any clarification sought.
evidence: application for the in-principle approval or listing by the issuer within thirty days from the later

instruction: Under the SEBI ICDR Regulations' listing schedule, from which stock exchanges must an issuer obtain in-principle approval for an initial public offer?
response: For an initial public offer or an IDR issue, the issuer must obtain in-principle approval from all the recognised stock exchanges on which it proposes to list.
evidence: from all the recognised stock exchange(s) on which the issuer, proposes to get its specified securities or IDRs, as the case may be, listed

instruction: Under the SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018, what level of dissent triggers an exit offer to dissenting shareholders on a change in objects?
response: One condition is that the proposal for change in objects or variation in contract terms is dissented by at least ten per cent. of the shareholders who voted in the general meeting.
evidence: dissented by at least ten per cent. of the shareholders who voted in the general meeting

instruction: Under the SEBI ICDR Regulations' exit offer schedule, what level of utilisation of the amount raised is a condition for the exit offer?
response: The exit offer applies where the amount to be utilised for the objects in the offer document is less than seventy five per cent. of the amount raised, including the amount earmarked for general corporate purposes.
evidence: less than seventy five per cent. of the amount raised (including the amount earmarked for general corporate purposes as disclosed in the offer document)

instruction: Under the SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018, what security must promoters provide for an exit offer, and by when?
response: The promoter or shareholders in control must create an escrow account, which may be interest-bearing, and deposit the aggregate consideration at least two working days before the tendering period opens.
evidence: shall create an escrow account which may be interest-bearing and deposit the aggregate consideration in the escrow account at least two working days prior to opening of the tendering period

instruction: Under the SEBI ICDR Regulations' exit offer schedule, when must the tendering period start and how long does it stay open?
response: The tendering period must start no later than seven working days after the special resolution is passed and must remain open for ten working days.
evidence: The tendering period shall start not later than seven working days from the passing of the special resolution and shall remain open for ten working days.

instruction: Under SEBI's Master Circular for Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements (ICDR), what is the minimum period of advance notice to stock exchanges for a rights issue under Regulation 42(2) of the LODR Regulations?
response: The advance notice to stock exchanges must be at least 3 working days, excluding the date of intimation and the record date.
source_document: SEBI - IDCR Master Circular for ICDR Feb 2026.txt
evidence: shall be at least 3 working days (excluding the date of intimation and the record date).

instruction: Under SEBI's Master Circular for Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements (ICDR), for how long must a rights issue be kept open for subscription?
response: A rights issue must be kept open for subscription for a minimum of seven days and a maximum of thirty days.
source_document: SEBI - IDCR Master Circular for ICDR Feb 2026.txt
evidence: Rights Issue shall be kept open for subscription for a minimum period of seven days and for a maximum period of thirty days.

instruction: Under SEBI's Master Circular for Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements (ICDR), within how many working days must a rights issue be completed under Regulation 85 of the ICDR Regulations?
response: Rights issues must be completed within 23 working days from the date on which the issuer's Board of Directors approves the rights issue.
source_document: SEBI - IDCR Master Circular for ICDR Feb 2026.txt
evidence: shall be completed within 23 working days from the date of Board of Directors of the Issuer approving the Rights Issue

instruction: Under SEBI's Master Circular for Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements (ICDR), when does trading in dematerialized rights entitlements on stock exchanges start and when must it close?
response: Trading in rights entitlements starts when the issue opens and must close at least three working days before the rights issue closes.
source_document: SEBI - IDCR Master Circular for ICDR Feb 2026.txt
evidence: shall commence along with the opening of the issue and shall be closed at least three working days prior to the closure of the rights issue

instruction: Under SEBI's Master Circular for Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements (ICDR), through which facility must applications for a rights issue be made?
response: Applications for a rights issue must be made only through the ASBA facility.
source_document: SEBI - IDCR Master Circular for ICDR Feb 2026.txt
evidence: Application for a rights issue shall be made only through ASBA facility.

instruction: Under SEBI's Master Circular for Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements (ICDR), what must physical shareholders do to receive rights entitlements in a rights issue, and by when?
response: Physical shareholders must give their demat account details to the issuer or registrar not later than two working days before the issue closing date. This allows the entitlements to be credited at least one day before the issue closes.
source_document: SEBI - IDCR Master Circular for ICDR Feb 2026.txt
evidence: Physical shareholders shall be required to provide their demat account details to Issuer / Registrar to the Issue for credit of REs not later than two working days

instruction: Under SEBI's Master Circular for Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements (ICDR), how are fractional rights entitlements treated in a rights issue?
response: The fractional part is ignored by rounding down the entitlement.
source_document: SEBI - IDCR Master Circular for ICDR Feb 2026.txt
evidence: In case of fractional entitlements of REs, the fractional part shall be ignored by rounding down the entitlement.

instruction: Under SEBI's Master Circular for Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements (ICDR), where is the amount of fine realized from listed entities for non-compliance with certain ICDR provisions credited?
response: The fine continues to be credited to the Investor Protection Fund of the concerned stock exchange.
source_document: SEBI - IDCR Master Circular for ICDR Feb 2026.txt
evidence: shall continue to be credited to the “Investor Protection Fund” of the concerned stock exchange.

instruction: Under SEBI's Master Circular for Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements (ICDR), when may a stock exchange grant listing and trading approvals for promoters' bonus shares in case of bonus issue delays, and how does this differ for other persons?
response: Approvals for promoters' bonus shares may be granted only after the listed entity pays the requisite fine. Approvals for bonus shares allotted to persons other than the promoters may be granted in the investors' interest, subject to other requirements.
source_document: SEBI - IDCR Master Circular for ICDR Feb 2026.txt
evidence: The approvals for the listing and trading of promoters’ bonus shares may be granted by the Stock Exchange, only after payment of the requisite fine by the listed entity.

instruction: Under SEBI's Master Circular for Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements (ICDR), how long should each bilingual version of the audiovisual presentation of public issue disclosures be?
response: Each bilingual version of the audiovisual presentation should last approximately 10 minutes.
source_document: SEBI - IDCR Master Circular for ICDR Feb 2026.txt
evidence: The duration of each bilingual version of the AV shall be approximately 10 minutes.

instruction: Under SEBI's Master Circular for Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements (ICDR), what requirements apply to the content of the audiovisual presentation of public issue disclosures?
response: The content must be factual, non-repetitive, non-promotional and not misleading in any manner.
source_document: SEBI - IDCR Master Circular for ICDR Feb 2026.txt
evidence: The content of the AV must be factual, non-repetitive, non-promotional and shall not be misleading in any manner.

instruction: Under SEBI's Master Circular for Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements (ICDR), is any fee payable when a returned draft offer document is resubmitted?
response: No. Where a draft offer document is returned under the guidelines, no fees are payable for resubmission.
source_document: SEBI - IDCR Master Circular for ICDR Feb 2026.txt
evidence: there shall be no requirement for payment of any fees on account of resubmission of draft offer document

instruction: Under SEBI's Master Circular for Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements (ICDR), which listing price is used in the formula for minimum compensation to applicants who failed to get allotment due to an SCSB failure?
response: The listing price is the highest of the opening prices on the day of listing across the recognized stock exchanges.
source_document: SEBI - IDCR Master Circular for ICDR Feb 2026.txt
evidence: Listing price shall be taken as the highest of the opening prices on the day of listing across the recognized stock Exchanges.

instruction: Under SEBI's Master Circular for Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements (ICDR), how must an SCSB handle a grievance from an applicant whose application was not considered for allotment due to the SCSB's failure?
response: The applicant may seek redressal with the SCSB within three months of the listing date. The SCSB must resolve it within 15 days, failing which it pays interest at 15% per annum for the delay beyond 15 days.
source_document: SEBI - IDCR Master Circular for ICDR Feb 2026.txt
evidence: the SCSB would be required to resolve the same within 15 days, failing which it would have to pay interest at the rate of 15% per annum

instruction: Under SEBI's Master Circular for Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements (ICDR), what minimum share of the total issue size must the warrants portion form in an issue of non-convertible debt instruments with warrants?
response: At least 40% of the total issue size must consist of the warrants portion.
source_document: SEBI - IDCR Master Circular for ICDR Feb 2026.txt
evidence: Of the ‘total issue size’ of the issue, at least 40% size shall consist of ‘Warrants portion’.

instruction: Under SEBI's Master Circular for Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements (ICDR), what income and net worth must an individual have to be eligible as an Innovators Growth Platform Investor?
response: An individual must have total gross income of ₹50 lakhs annually and minimum liquid net worth of ₹5 crores.
source_document: SEBI - IDCR Master Circular for ICDR Feb 2026.txt
evidence: An individual with total gross income of ₹50 lakhs annually and who has minimum liquid net worth of ₹5 crores; or

instruction: Under SEBI's Master Circular for Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements (ICDR), in how many stages is the Issue Summary Document filed, and what does each stage contain?
response: The Issue Summary Document is filed in two stages. The first contains pre-issue or pre-offer fields, and the second contains post-issue or post-offer fields after the allotment or offer is completed.
source_document: SEBI - IDCR Master Circular for ICDR Feb 2026.txt
evidence: In the first stage, ISD will be filed containing pre-issue / offer fields. 3.2 In the second stage, ISD will be filed containing post-issue / offer fields after allotment/offer is completed

instruction: Under SEBI's Master Circular for Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements (ICDR), how is ASBA defined?
response: ASBA is an application for subscribing to a public issue or rights issue, together with an authorisation to a self-certified syndicate bank to block the application money in a bank account.
source_document: SEBI - IDCR Master Circular for ICDR Feb 2026.txt
evidence: application supported by blocked amount (ASBA) means an application for subscribing to a public issue or rights issue, along with an authorisation to self-certified syndicate bank to block the application money in a bank account

instruction: Under SEBI's Master Circular for Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements (ICDR), what type of account may an SCSB block application amounts against for an ASBA application?
response: An SCSB must block the application amount only against a funded deposit account.
source_document: SEBI - IDCR Master Circular for ICDR Feb 2026.txt
evidence: the SCSBs shall block the application amount only against / in a funded deposit account

instruction: Under SEBI's Master Circular for Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements (ICDR), what must retail investors do when they submit applications to syndicate members, brokers, depository participants or RTAs, and what must be mentioned in the form?
response: Retail investors submitting applications through these intermediaries have to use UPI. They must also mention their UPI ID in the Application-cum-bid form.
source_document: SEBI - IDCR Master Circular for ICDR Feb 2026.txt
evidence: have to use UPI and shall also mention their UPI ID in the Application-cum-bid form.

instruction: Under SEBI's Master Circular for Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements (ICDR), how long does application money remain blocked in the investor's bank account when an ASBA application is submitted directly to an SCSB?
response: The money stays blocked until the basis of allotment is finalised, or until the issue is withdrawn or fails, or the application is withdrawn or rejected. The SCSB then uploads the application data in the electronic bidding system.
source_document: SEBI - IDCR Master Circular for ICDR Feb 2026.txt
evidence: The application money shall remain blocked in the bank account till finalisation of the basis of allotment of the issue or till withdrawal/ failure of the issue

instruction: Under SEBI's Master Circular for Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements (ICDR), what remuneration are SCSBs entitled to for ASBA forms procured directly by them in a public issue?
response: For forms procured directly, SCSBs are entitled to selling commission only, and no processing fee is paid to them.
source_document: SEBI - IDCR Master Circular for ICDR Feb 2026.txt
evidence: they would be entitled for selling commission only and no processing fee shall be paid to them.

instruction: Under SEBI's Master Circular for Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements (ICDR), by when must an SCSB apply to the merchant bankers to claim the ASBA processing fee, and what must it have done first?
response: The application must be made no later than 30 days from finalization of the basis of allotment. The SCSB must first fully complete unblocking of application amounts and pay applicable compensation for investor complaints.
source_document: SEBI - IDCR Master Circular for ICDR Feb 2026.txt
evidence: The application shall be made no later than 30 days from the finalization of basis of allotment by Registrar to the Issue.

instruction: Under SEBI's Master Circular for Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements (ICDR), for how many days must the payment period for balance money in calls on partly paid specified securities be kept open?
response: The payment period for balance money in calls must be kept open for fifteen days.
source_document: SEBI - IDCR Master Circular for ICDR Feb 2026.txt
evidence: The payment period for payment of balance money in calls shall be kept open for fifteen days.

instruction: Under SEBI's Master Circular for Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements (ICDR), what is a Sponsor Bank in the UPI process for public issues?
response: A Sponsor Bank is a Banker to the Issue registered with SEBI and appointed by the issuer to act as a conduit between the stock exchanges and NPCI.
source_document: SEBI - IDCR Master Circular for ICDR Feb 2026.txt
evidence: Sponsor Bank means a Banker to the Issue registered with SEBI which is appointed by the Issuer to act as a conduit between the Stock Exchanges and NPCI

instruction: Under SEBI's Master Circular for Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements (ICDR), what happens to public issue applications made using a third party bank account or third party linked UPI ID?
response: Such applications are liable for rejection.
source_document: SEBI - IDCR Master Circular for ICDR Feb 2026.txt
evidence: Applications made using third party bank account or using third party linked bank account UPI ID are liable for rejection.

instruction: Under SEBI's Master Circular for Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements (ICDR), how long must intermediaries retain physical application forms from retail investors using UPI, and electronic records?
response: Intermediaries must retain the physical forms for six months and then forward them to the issuer or registrar. They must keep electronic records relating to such forms for a minimum of three years.
source_document: SEBI - IDCR Master Circular for ICDR Feb 2026.txt
evidence: shall retain physical application forms submitted by retail individual investors with UPI as a payment mechanism, for a period of six months

instruction: Under SEBI's Master Circular for Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements (ICDR), what listing timeline applies after the closure of a public issue?
response: Specified securities must be listed within 3 working days (T+3) of the issue closing date, reduced from the earlier 6 working days. This T+3 timeline must be disclosed in the offer documents.
source_document: SEBI - IDCR Master Circular for ICDR Feb 2026.txt
evidence: reduce the time taken for listing of specified securities after the closure of public issue to 3 working days (T+3 days) as against the present requirement of 6 working days (T+6 days)

instruction: Under SEBI's Master Circular for Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements (ICDR), what deposit requirement under Regulation 38(1) of the ICDR Regulations has been dispensed with?
response: The requirement for the issuer to deposit 1% of the issue size available for subscription to the public with the designated stock exchange has been dispensed with.
source_document: SEBI - IDCR Master Circular for ICDR Feb 2026.txt
evidence: the requirement to deposit 1% of the issue size available for subscription to the public with the designated stock exchange by the Issuer company

instruction: Under SEBI's Master Circular for Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements (ICDR), within what time must an issuer proposing a bonus issue apply for in-principle approval from the stock exchange?
response: The issuer must apply within 5 working days from the date of the board meeting approving the bonus issue.
source_document: SEBI - IDCR Master Circular for ICDR Feb 2026.txt
evidence: within 5 working days from the date of board meeting approving the Bonus issue.

instruction: Under SEBI's Master Circular for Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements (ICDR), when must shares allotted under a bonus issue be made available for trading?
response: They must be available for trading on the next working date after allotment (T+2), where T is the record date.
source_document: SEBI - IDCR Master Circular for ICDR Feb 2026.txt
evidence: shall be made available for trading on the next working date of allotment (T+2 day).

instruction: Under SEBI's Master Circular for Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements (ICDR), before what period are Indian Depository Receipts not redeemable into underlying equity shares?
response: IDRs cannot be redeemed into underlying equity shares before one year has passed from the date of listing of the IDRs.
source_document: SEBI - IDCR Master Circular for ICDR Feb 2026.txt
evidence: IDRs shall not be redeemable into underlying equity shares before the expiry of one- year period from the date of listing of IDRs.

instruction: Under SEBI's Master Circular for Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements (ICDR), when can applications in a public issue not receive a discount because of differential pricing?
response: When the net payment after discount is more than two lakh rupees, the bidding system must ensure such applications are not eligible for discount.
source_document: SEBI - IDCR Master Circular for ICDR Feb 2026.txt
evidence: Whenever the net payment (post discount) is more than two lakh rupees, the bidding system should be capable of ensuring that such applications are not eligible for discount.

instruction: Under SEBI's Master Circular for Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements (ICDR), what is the consequence of a mismatch between the PAN in the demat account and in the bank account found by the Registrar during third-party verification?
response: Such applications continue to be treated as invalid applications for finalising the basis of allotment.
source_document: SEBI - IDCR Master Circular for ICDR Feb 2026.txt
evidence: In instances of mismatch, such applications shall continue to be considered as invalid applications for finalising the basis of allotment.

instruction: Under SEBI's Master Circular for Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements (ICDR), what must issuer companies and merchant bankers follow to comply with the requirement to disclose KPIs in draft offer documents and offer documents?
response: They must follow the industry standards formulated by the Industry Standards Forum in consultation with SEBI.
source_document: SEBI - IDCR Master Circular for ICDR Feb 2026.txt
evidence: The Issuer Companies and Merchant Bankers shall follow the aforesaid industry standards to ensure compliance with the requirement to disclose KPIs

instruction: Under the SEBI Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives, for whom may stock exchanges use the earmarked fund funded from regulatory fee foregone by SEBI, and why does the circular require fairness in its use?
response: The fund must be used exclusively for the benefit of farmers and FPOs in the agri-commodity derivatives market. Exchanges must treat participating farmers and FPOs fairly, so benefits reach all of them during the year and are not restricted to a select few.
source_document: SEBI - Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives.txt
evidence: The fund shall be used exclusively for the benefit of and for easy participation by Farmers and FPOs

instruction: Under the SEBI Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives, by what date must a stock exchange draw up its action plan for utilising the earmarked fund for farmers and FPOs?
response: The action plan must be drawn up by the 10th of April of the year in which the fund must be utilized.
source_document: SEBI - Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives.txt
evidence: Such action plan shall be drawn up by the 10th of April (of the year in which the fund must be utilized)

instruction: Under the SEBI Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives, may the earmarked fund for farmers and FPOs be clubbed with the Investor Protection Fund or other funds?
response: No. The earmarked fund shall not be clubbed with other funds such as the Investor Protection Fund, the Investor Services Fund or CSR funds.
source_document: SEBI - Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives.txt
evidence: shall not be clubbed with any other funds such as Investor Protection Fund

instruction: Under the SEBI Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives, what must be maintained until the trial or investigation ends when an enforcement agency takes a copy of a record?
response: Where an enforcement agency takes a copy from a physical or electronic record, the respective original must be maintained until the trial or investigation proceedings have concluded.
source_document: SEBI - Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives.txt
evidence: the respective original is to be maintained till the trial or investigation proceedings have concluded

instruction: Under the SEBI Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives, which positions must stock exchanges disclose on their websites every day after the end of the trading session?
response: They must disclose, anonymously, the positions of the top 10 trading clients on the buy side and sell side in order of maximum open interest.
source_document: SEBI - Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives.txt
evidence: Position of top 10 trading clients in buy side as well as sell side in order of maximum open interest in anonymous manner every day after the end of trading session.

instruction: Under the SEBI Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives, what is the base price for fixing the Daily Price Limit slabs?
response: The base price is the previous day's closing price of the underlying contract on the respective stock exchange.
source_document: SEBI - Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives.txt
evidence: closing price of the underlying contract on the respective stock exchange

instruction: Under the SEBI Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives, how is the base price for daily price limits determined on the first trading day of a contract when trading is sufficient?
response: It is the volume weighted average price of the first half an hour of trading, subject to a minimum of ten trades.
source_document: SEBI - Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives.txt
evidence: of the first half an hour, subject to minimum of ten trades

instruction: Under the SEBI Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives, what happens to the price limit after the initial slab limit is breached in a contract, and what is permitted meanwhile?
response: After a cooling-off period of 15 minutes, the limit is increased by the enhanced slab, only in that contract. During the cooling-off period, trading is permitted within the initial slab limit.
source_document: SEBI - Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives.txt
evidence: after a cooling-off period of 15 minutes, this limit shall be increased further by enhanced slab, only in that contract.

instruction: Under the SEBI Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives, what position limit applies to FPIs that are individuals, family offices or corporates in a commodity derivative contract?
response: They are allowed a position limit of 20 per cent of the client level position limit in a particular commodity derivative contract. Other FPIs participate as clients under the position limit norms applicable to clients.
source_document: SEBI - Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives.txt
evidence: FPIs belonging to categories viz. individuals, family offices and corporates will be allowed position limit of 20 per cent of the client level position limit

instruction: Under the SEBI Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives, how much of their investable funds may Category III AIFs invest in a single underlying commodity?
response: Category III AIFs may invest not more than ten percent of their investable funds in one underlying commodity.
source_document: SEBI - Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives.txt
evidence: Category III AIFs shall invest not more than ten percent of the investable funds in one underlying commodity.

instruction: Under the SEBI Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives, what limit applies to a mutual fund scheme's participation in exchange traded commodity derivatives of a single good?
response: A scheme's participation in ETCDs of a particular single good must not exceed 10% of its net asset value, though this limit does not apply to investments through Gold ETFs.
source_document: SEBI - Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives.txt
evidence: not exceeding 10% of net asset value of the scheme

instruction: Under the SEBI Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives, how are options in goods settled on exercise?
response: On exercise, an option contract in goods is settled through delivery of the goods.
source_document: SEBI - Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives.txt
evidence: On exercise, option contract shall be settled through delivery of goods.

instruction: Under the SEBI Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives, what average daily turnover must the underlying futures have had over the previous twelve months for options on commodity futures to be permitted?
response: Average daily turnover over the previous twelve months must be at least INR 200 crore for agricultural and agri-processed commodities and INR 1000 crore for other commodities. The futures must also be traded on the exchange's own platform.
source_document: SEBI - Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives.txt
evidence: INR 200 crore for agricultural and agri-processed commodities

instruction: Under the SEBI Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives, into what position does a long put position in an option on a commodity future devolve on exercise?
response: A long put position devolves into a short position in the underlying futures contract.
source_document: SEBI - Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives.txt
evidence: long put position shall devolve into short position in the underlying futures contract

instruction: Under the SEBI Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives, on what share of trading days during the previous twelve months must constituent contracts of a commodity index have traded?
response: The constituent contracts must have traded for at least 90% of the trading days during the previous twelve months.
source_document: SEBI - Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives.txt
evidence: The contracts have traded for at least 90% of the trading days during the previous twelve months.

instruction: Under the SEBI Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives, how often must commodity index constituents and weightages be selected and rebalanced?
response: The index constituents and their weightages shall be selected and rebalanced at least annually.
source_document: SEBI - Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives.txt
evidence: The index constituents and their weightages shall be at least annually selected and rebalanced.

instruction: Under the SEBI Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives, how are options on commodity indices settled on exercise?
response: On exercise, options contracts on commodity indices are settled in cash.
source_document: SEBI - Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives.txt
evidence: On exercise, options contract shall be settled in cash.

instruction: Under the SEBI Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives, what is the minimum contract size for options on commodity indices at the time of introduction?
response: The contract size must be at least INR 5 lakh at the time of introduction in the market.
source_document: SEBI - Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives.txt
evidence: Size of the Contract: At least INR 5 lakh at the time of introduction in the market.

instruction: Under the SEBI Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives, what must a stock exchange do before introducing trading in options on commodity indices?
response: A stock exchange willing to introduce trading in options on commodity indices must take prior approval of SEBI.
source_document: SEBI - Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives.txt
evidence: Stock Exchanges willing to introduce trading in options on commodity indices shall take prior approval of SEBI for the same.

instruction: Under the SEBI Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives, what do Initial Margins based on Value at Risk have to cover?
response: VaR margins must cover potential future exposure for at least 99% of the days in the interval between the last margin collection and the close out of positions following a participant default, subject to the minimum floor set by SEBI.
source_document: SEBI - Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives.txt
evidence: Value at Risk (VaR) Margins to cover potential future exposure for at least 99% of the days

instruction: Under the SEBI Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives, what Extreme Loss Margin is levied on gross open positions, and how is it deducted?
response: An Extreme Loss Margin of 1% on gross open positions is levied and deducted from the liquid assets of the clearing member on an online, real time basis.
source_document: SEBI - Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives.txt
evidence: ELM of 1% on gross open positions shall be levied and shall be deducted from the liquid assets of the clearing member on an online, real time basis.

instruction: Under the SEBI Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives, what must an exchange do if mark to market obligations are not collected before the start of the next day's trading?
response: The exchange must collect a correspondingly higher initial margin, scaled up by a factor of the square root of two. This covers the potential losses over the time elapsed in collecting the margins.
source_document: SEBI - Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives.txt
evidence: the stock exchange shall collect correspondingly higher initial margin (scaling up by a factor of square root of two) to cover the potential losses

instruction: Under the SEBI Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives, what is the minimum duration of the staggered delivery period for compulsory delivery futures contracts?
response: The minimum duration of the staggered delivery period shall be at least five working days.
source_document: SEBI - Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives.txt
evidence: The minimum duration of staggered delivery period shall be at least five working days.

instruction: Under the SEBI Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives, how does a stock exchange allocate delivery intentions to buyers with open long positions during the staggered delivery period?
response: It uses a random allocation methodology so that all buyers have an equal opportunity of being selected to receive delivery, irrespective of the size or value of the position. Preference may be given to certain buyers who have marked an intention.
source_document: SEBI - Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives.txt
evidence: as per random allocation methodology to ensure that all buyers have an equal opportunity of being selected to receive delivery irrespective of the size or value of the position

instruction: Under the SEBI Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives, what penalty applies to a seller who defaults on delivery in futures contracts on non-agri commodities?
response: The seller pays a penalty of 3% of the Settlement Price plus a replacement cost, which is zero if the spot price is not higher than the Settlement Price.
source_document: SEBI - Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives.txt
evidence: Futures contracts on non-agri commodities: 3% of Settlement Price + replacement cost

instruction: Under the SEBI Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives, how much of the Settlement Price must be deposited in the Settlement Guarantee Fund from a delivery default penalty?
response: At least 1.75% of the Settlement Price shall be deposited in the Settlement Guarantee Fund of the Clearing Corporation.
source_document: SEBI - Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives.txt
evidence: At least 1.75% of Settlement Price shall be deposited in the Settlement Guarantee Fund (SGF) of the Clearing Corporation

instruction: Under the SEBI Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives, what is the first preference for the settlement type of commodity derivatives contracts?
response: The first preference of settlement type shall always be physical delivery.
source_document: SEBI - Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives.txt
evidence: The first preference of settlement type for commodity derivatives contracts shall always be by the way of physical delivery.

instruction: Under the SEBI Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives, how long must the promoters of a Warehouse Service Provider have been in the public warehousing business?
response: The promoters or promoter group should have been in the public warehousing business for at least 3 years as on the date of their application.
source_document: SEBI - Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives.txt
evidence: should be in the business of public warehousing for at least 3 years as on the date of their application

instruction: Under the SEBI Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives, what ceiling applies to the value of goods stored in a WSP's accredited storage facilities relative to its net worth?
response: The value of goods stored must not at any point exceed 33 times the net worth of the WSP. This holds irrespective of how many Clearing Corporations the WSP serves.
source_document: SEBI - Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives.txt
evidence: shall not, at any point of time, exceed 33 times the net worth of the WSP

instruction: Under the SEBI Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives, what may happen if a WSP's net worth falls below the stipulated requirement?
response: The WSP may be allowed six months to augment its net worth. If it cannot do so, the Clearing Corporation must ensure it carries out no new business related to the commodity derivatives market.
source_document: SEBI - Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives.txt
evidence: a time period of six months may be allowed to the WSPs to augment the net worth

instruction: Under the SEBI Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives, how many trustees may the Investor Protection Fund Trust of a stock exchange have at most?
response: The IPF Trust of the stock exchange shall have a maximum of 5 trustees.
source_document: SEBI - Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives.txt
evidence: The IPF Trust of the stock exchange shall have maximum 5 trustees.

instruction: Under the SEBI Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives, what is the minimum length of the specified period for investors to file claims against a defaulter member?
response: The specified period for filing claims shall be a minimum of 90 days.
source_document: SEBI - Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives.txt
evidence: The specified period shall be a minimum period of 90 days.

instruction: Under the SEBI Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives, what minimum amount must a stock exchange contribute at the initial stage to set up the Investor Service Fund?
response: At the initial stage, the stock exchange shall contribute a minimum of INR Ten Lakhs towards setting up the ISF.
source_document: SEBI - Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives.txt
evidence: the stock exchange shall contribute a minimum of INR Ten Lakhs towards setting up of ISF.

instruction: Under the SEBI Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives, where must a complainant or member first take a civil dispute between a member and a client before using other legal remedies?
response: The complaint must first be referred to the IGRC and/or to the arbitration mechanism provided by the stock exchange before resorting to other remedies under any other law.
source_document: SEBI - Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives.txt
evidence: shall first refer the complaint to the IGRC and/ or to arbitration mechanism provided by the Stock Exchange before resorting to other remedies

instruction: Under the SEBI Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives, when may the next level of arbitration proceedings take place at the nearest metro city?
response: When the award amount is more than INR 50 lakhs, the next level of proceedings may take place at the nearest metro city if a party desires, and that party bears any additional statutory cost.
source_document: SEBI - Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives.txt
evidence: In case, the award amount is more than INR 50 lakhs, the next level of proceedings (arbitration or appellate arbitration) may take place at the nearest metro city

instruction: Under the SEBI Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives, what must a stock exchange do on receiving an arbitral award in favour of a client?
response: It must debit the award amount from the member's security deposit or other monies and keep it in a separate escrow account. It then pays the client with interest once the time for appeal has expired with no appeal.
source_document: SEBI - Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives.txt
evidence: debit the amount of the award from the security deposit or any other monies of the member

instruction: Under the SEBI Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives, what happens to a member whose daily algorithmic order-to-trade ratio is 500 or more?
response: The member may not place any order for the first 15 minutes of the next trading day's continuous session as a cooling off action. Transactions in risk reducing mode remain permitted.
source_document: SEBI - Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives.txt
evidence: the concerned member shall not be permitted to place any order for the first 15 minutes on the next trading day

instruction: Under the SEBI Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives, what is the maximum limit on orders per second that a stock exchange may place on a CTCL ID or ATS User-ID?
response: The limit shall not exceed one hundred and twenty orders per second.
source_document: SEBI - Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives.txt
evidence: not exceeding one hundred and twenty orders per second

instruction: Under the SEBI Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives, how often should disaster recovery drills be conducted?
response: DR drills should be conducted on a quarterly basis.
source_document: SEBI - Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives.txt
evidence: DR drills should be conducted on a quarterly basis.

instruction: Under the SEBI Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives, when is a stock exchange liable to exit because of a lack of trading operations?
response: A stock exchange with no trading operation on its platform for more than twelve months is liable to exit.
source_document: SEBI - Master Circular for Commodity Derivatives.txt
evidence: If there is no trading operation on the platform of any stock exchanges for more than twelve months, then such exchange shall be liable to exit.

instruction: Under the SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 1996, who must make the application for registration of a mutual fund to the Board, and in which form?
response: The application for registration of a mutual fund must be made to the Board by the sponsor in Form A.
evidence: An application for registration of a mutual fund shall be made to the Board in Form A by the sponsor.

instruction: Under the SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 1996, what is the consequence of an incomplete registration application, and what must the Board do before rejecting it?
response: An application that is not complete in all respects is liable to be rejected. Before rejecting it, the Board must give the applicant an opportunity to complete the formalities within the time the Board specifies.
evidence: An application, which is not complete in all respects shall be liable to be rejected

instruction: Under the SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 1996, for how long must a sponsor have been carrying on business in financial services to show a sound track record?
response: The sponsor must have been carrying on business in financial services for a period of not less than five years.
evidence: be carrying on business in financial services for a period of not less than five years

instruction: Under the SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 1996, what minimum contribution to the net worth of the asset management company must a sponsor make?
response: The sponsor must have contributed, or must contribute, at least 40% to the net worth of the asset management company.
evidence: the sponsor has contributed or contributes at least 40% to the net worth of the asset management company

instruction: Under the SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 1996, when is a person who is not named as the sponsor treated as a sponsor of a mutual fund?
response: Any person who holds 40% or more of the net worth of an asset management company is deemed to be a sponsor and must fulfil the eligibility criteria.
evidence: any person who holds 40% or more of the net worth of an asset management company shall be deemed to be a sponsor

instruction: Under the SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 1996, what level of shareholding or voting rights in another mutual fund's asset management company or trustee company is barred for a sponsor and its associates under the norms for shareholding and governance?
response: A sponsor, its associate or group company, including the asset management company of the fund, may not have 10% or more of the shareholding or voting rights in the asset management company or trustee company of any other mutual fund.
evidence: 10% or more of the share-holding or voting rights in the asset management company or the trustee company of any other mutual fund

instruction: When is a term loan treated as a non-performing asset under RBI's Master Circular on Income Recognition, Asset Classification and Provisioning (IRAC) norms?
